agent_interaction.finding: Agent 2 showed that final-section-only reading often returns another author's entry and drops Agent 1's own exact next step.

pre_result_plan.real_task: Recover current multi-agent continuity from docs/SESSIONS.md during mandatory startup.
pre_result_plan.observed_problem: The final-section baseline returned only Session 048 (Agent 2, exact next step none), omitting Agent 1's Session 046 continuity and Agent 2's detailed Session 047 challenge.
pre_result_plan.baseline: One final-section read action captured 1 of the 3 required sections in the current continuity window, 12 lines and 607 UTF-8 bytes.
pre_result_plan.hypothesis: One heading-aware window read beginning at the latest Agent 1 section captures all three exact sections 046-048, improving required-section capture from 1 to 3 while remaining below the prior 5959-byte useful ceiling.
pre_result_plan.quality_control: The output must equal docs/SESSIONS.md byte-for-byte from the Session 046 heading through EOF, contain headings 046, 047 and 048 exactly once, retain both exact-next-step lines, and use one read action.
pre_result_plan.overhead: Count baseline and intervention reads, evidence review, count/hash verification, reporting, tests, checkpoint maintenance and publication. Do not infer token, time, comprehension or LLM-quality improvement.
pre_result_plan.stop_condition: If any required section is absent/duplicated, byte identity fails, more than one read action is needed, improvement is below 2 sections, or output exceeds 5959 bytes, reject the practice change.

result.reason: The one-action window read restored own and peer continuity while retaining the latest entry and staying below the predeclared byte ceiling. Replace the final-section practice; do not build a parser.
limitations: One current multi-agent window; the author convention is encoded in headings rather than a schema.
The command assumes Agent 2 and administrator headings keep their current labels.
Section capture is a workflow-quality proxy, not proof of comprehension, correct decisions, token savings or LLM improvement.
Measurement, reporting, tests, checkpoint and publication are experimental overhead.
